content: Quinine exerts its effects by inhibiting nucleic acid synthesis, protein synthesis, and glycolysis in Plasmodium falciparum. Additionally, it has the ability to bind with hemozoin within parasitized erythrocytes. However, the exact mechanism by which quinine sulfate achieves its antimalarial effects remains incompletely understood. Quinine sulfate primarily targets the blood schizont stage of P. falciparum. It does not exhibit gametocidal activity and has minimal impact on the sporozoite or pre-erythrocytic stages of the parasite's life cycle. Strains of P. falciparum with reduced susceptibility to quinine can emerge through selection in vivo. Cases of P. falciparum malaria that are clinically resistant to quinine have been documented in certain regions, including parts of South America, Southeast Asia, and Bangladesh.
